From cde6bcd584b1b910d6ee8d6eb968ea5d20815444 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2016 15:20:02 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: AMD: free memory on error

Static checkers complain if we don't free "adata" before returning.

Fixes: 7c31335a03b6 ('ASoC: AMD: add AMD ASoC ACP 2.x DMA driver')
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c b/sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c
index 3191e0a7d273..d1fb035f44db 100644
--- a/sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c
+++ b/sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c
@@ -635,6 +635,7 @@ static int acp_dma_open(struct snd_pcm_substream *substream)
 					    SNDRV_PCM_HW_PARAM_PERIODS);
 	if (ret < 0) {
 		dev_err(prtd->platform->dev, "set integer constraint failed\n");
+		kfree(adata);
 		return ret;
 	}
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `sound/soc/amd/acp-pcm-dma.c`**
- A line was added to free the memory allocated to `adata` using `kfree(adata);` before returning an error code in the `acp_dma_open` function. This change occurs after a check for a failed operation (`if (ret < 0)`), ensuring that if the operation fails, the allocated memory is properly released to prevent memory leaks.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a memory management issue identified by static checkers, which indicated that the memory allocated for `adata` was not being freed in the event of an error. By adding the `kfree(adata);` line, the patch ensures that the memory is released appropriately, thus improving the robustness of the code and preventing potential memory leaks when the function encounters an error. This change is directly related to the error handling logic within the `acp_dma_open` function.
